doc_title: Sustainability Accounting Standard: Chemicals
chunk_text: The entity shall disclose the total number of incidents of non-compliance associated with water quality permits, standards and regulations, including violations of a technology-based standard and exceedances of quantity or quality-based standards. The scope of disclosure includes incidents governed by applicable jurisdictional statutory permits and regulations, which include the discharge of a hazardous substance, violation of pre-treatment requirements or total maximum daily load (TMDL) exceedances. The scope of disclosure shall only include incidents of non-compliance that resulted in a formal enforcement action(s). Formal enforcement actions are defined as governmental actions that address a violation or threatened violation of water quantity or quality laws, regulations, policies or orders, and can result in administrative penalty orders, administrative orders and judicial actions, among others. Violations shall be disclosed, regardless of their measurement methodology or frequency, including violations for continuous and non-continuous discharges.
summary: Requirement to report formal enforcement actions and non-compliance incidents related to water quality and discharge permits.
tags: non-compliance, water permits, hazardous discharge, enforcement actions

doc_title: Sustainability Accounting Standard: Chemicals
chunk_text: The entity shall calculate and disclose (1) the total weight of hazardous waste generated, in metric tonnes. Hazardous wastes are defined in accordance with the applicable jurisdictional legal or regulatory frameworks where the waste was generated. The entity shall also calculate and disclose (2) the percentage of hazardous waste recycled as the weight of hazardous waste generated that was recycled, divided by the total weight in metric tonnes of hazardous waste generated. Hazardous waste that is reused, reclaimed or remanufactured shall be considered within the scope of recycled. Recycled, reused, reclaimed and remanufactured hazardous waste is defined in accordance with the applicable jurisdictional legal or regulatory frameworks where the waste was generated. Materials incinerated, including for energy recovery, shall not be considered within the scope of recycled. The entity shall disclose the frameworks used to define hazardous waste and recycled hazardous waste, and the quantities and percentages defined in accordance with each applicable framework.
summary: Requirement to report the total weight of hazardous waste generated and the percentage that is recycled, reused, or reclaimed.
tags: hazardous waste, recycling rate, waste generation, regulatory framework

doc_title: Sustainability Accounting Standard: Chemicals
chunk_text: The entity shall disclose (1) its total recordable incident rate (TRIR) for work-related injuries and illnesses and (2) its fatality rate for work-related fatalities. An injury or illness is considered a recordable incident if it results in death, days away from work, restricted work or transfer to another job, medical treatment beyond first aid, or loss of consciousness. All disclosed rates shall be calculated as: (statistic count × 200,000) / total number of hours worked by all employees in the year reported. The scope includes work-related incidents only, resulting from events or exposures in the work environment, including physical locations and equipment or materials used by the employee. The entity shall disclose the rates for direct employees, defined as individuals on the entity’s payroll, and contract employees, defined as individuals who are not on the entity’s payroll but whom the entity supervises or manages, including independent contractors and those employed by third parties.
summary: Mandatory disclosure of safety incident rates (TRIR) and fatalities for both direct and contract employees using a normalized formula.
tags: trir, fatality rate, contract workers, workplace safety

doc_title: Sustainability Accounting Standard: Chemicals
chunk_text: The entity shall discuss how it assesses, monitors and reduces workforce exposure to long-term (chronic) human health risks which may include: corrosives, hepatotoxins, nephrotoxins, neurotoxins, sensitisers, and known or suspected carcinogens, teratogens, mutagens and reprotoxins. The workforce includes any personnel conducting entity business on behalf of the entity, including all direct employees and contract employees. Relevant efforts to describe might include: automation of processes; completion of occupational exposure limit reviews; implementation of technology to limit harmful worker exposure; risk assessments and participation in long-term health studies; worker use of personal protective equipment; and phasing out, substituting or using safer alternative materials. The entity may describe its implementation of relevant safety management systems which may include the measurement of safety and health performance through metrics and obtaining third-party verification of compliance with relevant jurisdictional safety standards.
summary: Requirement to describe management strategies and monitoring for reducing workforce exposure to chronic health hazards and toxic substances.
tags: occupational exposure, carcinogens, ppe, safety management systems

doc_title: Sustainability Accounting Standard: Chemicals
chunk_text: The entity shall calculate and disclose (1) the percentage of products that contain Globally Harmonised System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS) Category 1 and 2 Health and Environmental Hazardous Substances. The categories of GHS Health Hazards include acute toxicity, skin corrosion/irritation, serious eye damage/eye irritation, respiratory or skin sensitization, germ cell mutagenicity, carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, and specific target organ toxicity. GHS Environmental Hazards include hazardous to the aquatic environment and hazardous to the ozone layer. The entity shall calculate the percentage as the revenue from products containing these substances divided by total revenue. The entity shall also disclose (2) the percentage of such products that have undergone a hazard assessment, defined as a process to identify, implement, document and communicate health, safety and environmental measures to manage risk so that products can be safely used for their intended purposes.
source_section_or_page: Safety & Environmental Stewardship of Chemicals, pp. 28-29
summary: Requirement to report the revenue percentage of products containing high-hazard chemicals and the status of their hazard assessments.
tags: ghs classification, hazardous substances, hazard assessment, revenue percentage

doc_title: Sustainability Accounting Standard: Chemicals
chunk_text: The entity shall discuss its strategy and approach to managing the production of materials, chemicals and substances that may be hazardous to human health or the environment, presenting concerns for consumers, customers, regulators or others. Relevant operational processes may include product formulation and design, product safety testing, risk characterisation, prioritisation of product risks, product labelling, product declarations (for example, material safety data sheets), and sharing of information on product risks. The entity shall also discuss communication processes used to share product information within the entity’s supply chain and management of new information on product risks. Additionally, the entity shall discuss its strategy to develop alternative processes and chemicals that reduce or avoid the use of substances hazardous to human health or the environment, including the use of relevant aspects of the 12 Principles of Green Chemistry.
source_section_or_page: Safety & Environmental Stewardship of Chemicals, pp. 29-30
summary: Requirement to describe strategies for managing chemicals of concern and the development of safer alternatives through supply chain communication.
tags: supply chain communication, msds, green chemistry, risk management

doc_title: Sustainability Accounting Standard: Chemicals
chunk_text: The entity shall disclose its process safety performance using these indicators: Process Safety Incidents Count (PSIC), Process Safety Total Incident Rate (PSTIR), and Process Safety Incident Severity Rate (PSISR), consistent with ANSI/API Recommended Practice 754. PSIC is defined as the total count of all incidents that meet the definition of a Tier 1 Process Safety Event (PSE). The scope includes PSEs occurring at entity-owned or entity-operated facilities and includes those affecting direct employees as well as contract employees. The entity shall describe incidents with a severity rating of Tier 1 or Tier 2, including root causes, outcomes and corrective actions implemented in response, such as technology improvements or operator training. Strong process safety management may reduce operational downtime, mitigate costs and regulatory risk, and ensure workforce productivity.
source_section_or_page: Operational Safety, Emergency Preparedness & Response, pp. 34-35
summary: Mandatory reporting of process safety incidents (Tier 1 and 2) and their severity rates for facilities and contract personnel.
tags: psic, tier 1 pse, root cause analysis, operational safety

doc_title: Sustainability Accounting Standard: Chemicals
chunk_text: The entity shall disclose the total number of transport incidents, defined consistent with applicable jurisdictional laws or regulations. A reportable transport incident is defined, irrespective of chemical products contribution, as an incident resulting in: a death or injury leading to intensive medical treatment or hospital stay; any release of more than 50 kg/L of dangerous goods or more than 1,000 kg/L of non-dangerous goods; any damage of more than 50,000 Euros resulting from a transport incident; or an incident leading to direct involvement of authorities, evacuation, or closure of public traffic routes. The entity shall report distribution incidents for all modes of product transport (road, rail or ship). The scope includes all distributions for which the entity has direct oversight as well as those contracted by the entity to a third party (Tier 1 contracts). The entity shall describe significant transport incidents, including root causes and corrective actions implemented in response.
source_section_or_page: Operational Safety, Emergency Preparedness & Response, p. 35
summary: Requirement to disclose transport and distribution incidents, including those managed by Tier 1 third-party contractors.
tags: transport safety, tier 1 contracts, dangerous goods, logistics risk

doc_title: Containers & Packaging Sustainability Accounting Standard
chunk_text: The entity shall disclose its gross global Scope 1 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions to the atmosphere of the seven GHGs covered under the Kyoto Protocol—carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), perfluorocarbons (PFCs), sulphur hexafluoride (SF6), and nitrogen trifluoride (NF3). Emissions of all GHGs shall be consolidated and disclosed in metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalents (CO2-e) and calculated in accordance with published 100-year time horizon global warming potential (GWP) values. Gross emissions are GHGs emitted into the atmosphere before accounting for offsets, credits or other similar mechanisms that have reduced or compensated for emissions. Scope 1 emissions are defined and shall be calculated according to the methodology contained in The Greenhouse Gas Protocol: A Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard (GHG Protocol), Revised Edition, March 2004, published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council on Sustainable Development (WRI/WBCSD).
summary: Requirement for packaging entities to report gross Scope 1 emissions in CO2-e using GHG Protocol methodologies without offsets.
tags: ghg protocol, carbon footprint, kyoto protocol, co2-e

doc_title: Containers & Packaging Sustainability Accounting Standard
chunk_text: The entity shall disclose (1) the total amount of energy it consumed as an aggregate figure, in gigajoules (GJ). The scope of energy consumption includes energy from all sources, including energy purchased from external sources and energy produced by the entity itself (self-generated). For example, direct fuel usage, purchased electricity, heating, cooling and steam energy all are included within the scope of energy consumption. The scope of energy consumption includes only energy directly consumed by the entity during the reporting period. In calculating energy consumption from fuels and biofuels, the entity shall use higher heating values (HHV), also known as gross calorific values (GCV), which are measured directly or taken from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). The entity shall disclose (2) the percentage of energy it consumed that was supplied from grid electricity. The percentage shall be calculated as purchased grid electricity consumption divided by total energy consumption.
summary: Requirement to disclose total energy consumption in gigajoules and the percentage of energy sourced from grid electricity.
tags: gigajoules, grid electricity, fuel usage, data normalization

doc_title: Containers & Packaging Sustainability Accounting Standard
chunk_text: Renewable energy is defined as energy from sources that are replenished at a rate greater than or equal to their rate of depletion, such as geothermal, wind, solar, hydro and biomass. The percentage shall be calculated as renewable energy consumption divided by total energy consumption. The scope of renewable energy includes renewable fuel the entity consumed, renewable energy the entity directly produced and renewable energy the entity purchased, if purchased through a renewable power purchase agreement (PPA) that explicitly includes renewable energy certificates (RECs) or Guarantees of Origin (GOs), a Green-e Energy Certified utility or supplier programme, or other green power products that explicitly include RECs or GOs. For any renewable electricity generated on site, any RECs and GOs shall be retained and retired or cancelled on behalf of the entity for the entity to claim them as renewable energy. For renewable PPAs, the agreement shall explicitly include and convey that RECs and GOs be retained or replaced and retired or cancelled on behalf of the entity.
summary: Criteria for calculating and claiming renewable energy consumption, including the mandatory retention and retirement of RECs and GOs.
tags: renewable energy, ppa, recs, green-e

doc_title: Containers & Packaging Sustainability Accounting Standard
chunk_text: The entity shall disclose the amount of water, in thousands of cubic metres, withdrawn from all sources. Water sources include surface water, groundwater, rainwater collected directly and stored by the entity, and water and wastewater obtained from municipal water supplies, water utilities or other

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: For formal methods of solicitation for goods, services or works (ITB, RFP) as well as EOIs and PQ leading to the short listing of suppliers, and processes to establish LTAs, the inclusion of the DRiVE supplier sustainability questionnaire is mandatory. DRiVE assesses suppliers across 10 different sustainability areas including policy, management systems, human rights, labour standards, equal opportunity, environment, health and safety, quality management, sub-contractors and code of conduct. Data is collected from suppliers during the tender process through the DRiVE Supplier Sustainability questionnaire and is supplemented with global datasets representing the industry, market and local context. Identified suppliers are subject to an inspection or verification process after which a Corrective Action & Preventive Action plan (CAPA) is issued including corrective actions for suppliers to implement on a voluntary basis.
summary: Mandatory requirement to include the DRiVE questionnaire in formal solicitations and shortlisting processes to assess supplier sustainability across 10 areas.
tags: drive questionnaire, sustainability assessment, supplier onboarding, corrective action

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: For formal methods of solicitation (ITB, RFP) for goods and services with an expected award amount above USD 1 million, as well as for the establishment of LTAs, the inclusion of at least 1 gender mainstreaming criterion and at least 1 relevant sustainable procurement technical criterion is mandatory. If the category is listed in Part 2, the sustainability criteria should be selected from the pre-identified list in the SP Framework Guidance & Resource Tool. Embedding sustainability considerations into the contract issued to the supplier will enable UNOPS to ensure that the outputs expected are achieved. This is a crucial requirement, especially for longer-term contracts with suppliers, such as LTAs, where the relationship is expected to last several years, or where the risk to UNOPS is deemed to be higher.
summary: Mandatory requirement for high-value awards and LTAs to include specific gender and technical sustainability evaluation criteria.
tags: award threshold, gender mainstreaming, technical criteria, lta

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: UNOPS considers that certain products and categories have a significant adverse impact on the environment or public health and as such should not be purchased by UNOPS business units. These products or categories are: (1) Single-use plastics, though health products specifically required by applicable regulatory frameworks are exempt; (2) Incandescent or fluorescent light bulbs, with exemptions for mandatory healthcare requirements; (3) Tobacco products; and (4) Diesel generators. In cases where the purchase of these categories are deemed necessary for successful project delivery, a waiver must be requested from the Director, PG. Any waiver request must be endorsed by the head of office, identify the justification for the waiver, and detail the specific circumstances applicable to the situation prior to launching the tender.
summary: List of prohibited product categories (single-use plastics, diesel generators, etc.) and the mandatory waiver process for necessary exceptions.
tags: single-use plastics, diesel generators, tobacco, waiver process

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: The SP Framework mandatory requirements apply to all UNOPS solicitation processes (RFQ, ITB, RFP) with an estimated value of USD 5,000 or above, and any request for expression of interest (EOI) or invitation for pre-qualification (PQ) used for short-listing purposes. There are specific exceptions, such as procurement processes done under Emergency procurement procedures (EPP), procurement further to pre-selection, call-off orders against LTAs established by UNOPS prior to 1st January 2020 or against LTAs established by other UN Agencies, and advisory procurement projects where UNOPS conducts the solicitation but is not responsible for signing the contract or disbursing funds. For all other processes meeting the value threshold, sustainability criteria must be incorporated as identified in the framework.
summary: Defined value thresholds and specific exceptions for the mandatory application of the Sustainable Procurement Framework.
tags: threshold, solicitation scope, exceptions, epp

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: UNOPS aims to enhance the diversity and inclusion of our supplier base through the UNOPS Possibilities (UP) programme. This programme has a focus on local Micro, Medium, Small Enterprises (MSMEs), women-owned businesses (WOB), disability-inclusive suppliers and other diverse suppliers, such as youth-owned businesses (YOB) or those belonging to indigenous or LGBTQI+ groups. Procurement practitioners may consider establishing longer-term contracts as these increase the opportunity to improve the sustainability of vendors over time. Practitioners may also divide large procurements into smaller lots to be more accessible to local MSMEs that may not have the capacity to bid for the entire requirement. Furthermore, it is permitted to designate a proportion of lots or subcontracts specifically for businesses that meet the characteristics of these special interest groups.
summary: Procurement strategies to support supplier diversity, including smaller lots and designated subcontracts for MSMEs and women-owned businesses.
tags: msme, women-owned business, disability inclusion, diverse suppliers

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: Disability-inclusive procurement addresses disability inclusion through policies that consider accessibility and do not create new barriers for persons with disabilities. This includes procuring accessible goods and services, ensuring that everyone benefits from features in our environment that prevent or remove barriers to functioning or using a service. Procurement practitioners must ensure that the procurement process itself is accessible for people with disabilities, by for instance issuing accessible solicitation documents and making the supplier-facing procurement systems accessible. Sustainability of infrastructure works is a priority, and designs used in the procurement process for building construction must comply with the UNOPS Design Planning Manual for Buildings, which covers environmental imperatives as well as access and egress (including accessibility considerations).
summary: Requirements for ensuring goods, services, and the procurement process itself are accessible to persons with disabilities.
tags: accessibility, infrastructure design, barrier removal, inclusive procurement

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: Requirements definitions shall address specific and relevant sustainability requirements through either precise technical, functional or performance specifications. Technical specifications should bear a link to the subject matter of the contract and should only include those requirements that are related to the production of the goods, services or works being procured. Procurement practitioners may specify both the materials to be used in production and/or the method of production or service delivery. For instance, a total cost of ownership methodology can be applied to compare different categories that yield the same desired outcome (e.g., generators and solar panels) to identify the most cost-effective and potentially most environmentally friendly solution. Evaluation criteria for certain product/service categories can include a requirement that evaluation will be done using this Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) methodology.
summary: Guidance on defining sustainability through technical specifications and the use of Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) in evaluation.
tags: technical specifications, production methods, tco, value for money

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: Evaluation criteria may require sustainable procurement technical competence to be demonstrated. In practical terms, this may require that the bidder: has previous experience in successfully executing contracts with similar requirements; employs or has access to personnel with the required educational and professional qualifications, practices and experience to deal with the sustainable procurement elements of the contract; owns or has access to the necessary technical equipment for environmental protection; and has the means to deliver on the sustainable procurement aspects of the contract. Once the contract is awarded, relevant sustainability clauses from the tender should be included in the contract. These clauses should be SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, Time-bound), for example, requiring packaging improvements such as using bulk shipment or predetermined reporting on sustainability criteria for the purchase in question.
summary: Criteria for evaluating a bidder's technical competence in sustainability and the use of SMART contract clauses to ensure performance.
tags: technical competence, supplier experience, smart clauses, reporting requirements

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: Sustainability requirements should be considered as early as possible in the procurement process, ideally identifying needs at the project design stage or the procurement planning stage. Market analysis helps understand existing solutions, international practices, and social, environmental, and economic risks or opportunities for a specific product or service. A sustainability risk assessment allows the identification of priority areas by assessing key spend data and specific procurement processes in the procurement plan. Prioritization should focus on sustainability elements that are important and relevant to the specific product or service group. Furthermore, procurement practitioners should consider whether goods or services need to be purchased at all, as alternative solutions like leasing or purchasing fewer units might be more cost-effective and lead to reduced waste and emissions.
summary: Importance of early consideration of sustainability, market analysis, and risk assessments to prioritize relevant procurement interventions.
tags: market analysis, risk assessment, prioritization, project design

doc_title: UNOPS Sustainable Procurement Framework
chunk_text: Including sustainability considerations in contract management activities allows the monitoring of sustainability performance, measuring impact, and enhancing supplier capacity to deliver against future contracts. Specific considerations at this stage include utilizing the DRiVE programme to engage suppliers through site inspections, response verifications, or voluntary Corrective Action & Preventive Action plans (CAPA). Procurement officials must regularly monitor the performance of the supplier during the contract period, with a particular focus on the sustainability requirements or KPIs included in the contract. Upon contract completion, the supplier performance evaluation (SPE) in oneUNOPS should be completed, including a rating and assessment of the supplier's sustainability delivery. This ensures accountability and identifies areas for continuous improvement within the supplier base.
summary: Monitoring of supplier sustainability performance during and after the contract through KPIs, DRiVE inspections, and formal evaluations.
tags: kpis, drive programme, supplier evaluation, site inspections

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: Unilever will verify alignment to and implementation of the RSP’s Mandatory Requirements through the use of supplier self-declaration, online assessments and – for designated high-risk countries and supplier types – independent verification including third-party audits. The implementation process will encompass a process suitable for small businesses as well as large businesses with well-established compliance programmes. Senior management are engaged and have oversight of the content and implementation of their compliance framework. This approach ensures that all suppliers, regardless of their size, are held accountable to the same fundamental principles through a tiered verification system that considers the specific risk profile of the supplier's location and business activities.
summary: Overview of Unilever's tiered supplier verification process, including self-declarations, online assessments, and third-party audits.
tags: self-declaration, online assessment, third-party audit, risk-based verification

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: There is a prohibition on any and all forms of bribery, corruption, extortion or embezzlement and there are adequate procedures in place to prevent bribery in all commercial dealings undertaken by the supplier. Procedures to ensure that all applicable laws and regulations are complied with by the supplier and its workers are tailored to the size and risk profile of the business. A regular risk assessment is undertaken to identify key compliance risks. Clear and effective internal training and/or guidelines are in place to embed a culture of integrity and mitigate key risks, for example; on gifts and hospitality, conflicts of interest, handling competitor information and anti-competitive behaviour. Such guidelines are readily available to the supplier’s workers.
summary: Mandatory anti-corruption requirements, including risk assessments, internal training, and tailored compliance procedures.
tags: anti-corruption, risk assessment, ethics training, integrity culture

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: All and any conflict of interest in any business dealings with Unilever, of which the supplier is aware, will be declared to Unilever to allow Unilever the opportunity to take appropriate action. Any ownership or beneficial interest in a supplier’s business by a government official, representative of a political party or a Unilever worker are declared to Unilever prior to any business relationship with Unilever being entered into. Gifts and hospitality with Unilever is kept reasonable in nature, entirely for the purpose of maintaining good business relations and not intended to influence in any way Unilever’s decisions about how Unilever awards future business. Gift giving should occur sparingly and always be legitimate and aligned with company policies.
summary: Requirement for suppliers to declare all actual or potential conflicts of interest, including ownership by government officials.
tags: conflict of interest, beneficial ownership, gifts and hospitality, transparency

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: The key components of the employer/worker relationship such as hours, overtime, pay, benefits, leave, disciplinary and grievance systems are freely agreed by both parties, documented in writing, and signed by the employer and worker. Suppliers shall ensure that the terms and conditions of employment contracts are in a language understood by the worker and are explained verbally if required. These policies and procedures are explained to workers upon hiring and contained in a workers’ manual, and workers are trained to understand and use them. Ongoing training practices are provided for all categories of workers to raise and broaden their skills to enable them to advance in their employment. This ensures that all workers, both permanent and casual, are provided with employment documents that respect their legal and contractual rights.
summary: Requirement for all employment terms to be documented in writing, signed, and provided in a language understood by the worker.
tags: employment contracts, worker handbook, legal rights, transparent terms

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: Mental and physical coercion, slavery and human trafficking are prohibited. Workers should not be required to pay a fee in connection with obtaining employment, including migrant workers or recruited workers supplied through an agency. Suppliers should be responsible for payment of all fees and expenses. Workers are not required to pay deposits in relation to their employment. Workers are not required to surrender their identification papers. Where the retention of identification papers is legally required, arrangements are made to ensure that workers can access their identification papers, are not prevented from leaving the workplace and that their papers are returned immediately upon cessation of employment. If you use labour brokers or agencies, ensure you fully understand their procedures and know they are not using forced or trafficked labour.
summary: Prohibition of forced labor, recruitment fees, and the retention of worker identification papers by suppliers or agencies.
tags: human trafficking, recruitment fees, identification papers, migrant workers

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: Under no circumstances will a supplier employ individuals under the age of 15 or under the local legal minimum age for work or mandatory schooling, whichever is higher. An employment policy is in place specifying the minimum age for employment, together with effective procedures and means of age verification to implement this policy. Age verification for job applicants is an important step in ensuring that you do not hire under-age workers. Document your process. In all circumstances the health and safety of young workers are considered and protected. This protection should preclude them from certain types of work such as hazardous or night work. Responsible remedial measures are immediately implemented whenever any breach of that policy is identified. If you use contract labour, ensure that your agency also has an age verification process.
summary: Mandatory minimum age requirements and the necessity of documented age verification procedures for all workers.
tags: age verification, minimum age, young workers, hazardous work

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: Workers receive a payslip for each pay period, clearly indicating the components of the compensation, including exact amounts for wages, benefits, incentives/bonuses and any deductions. Wages are paid on time and in full. All work is compensated according to at least the legal minimum standards or the appropriate prevailing industry standards, whichever is the higher. All legally mandated deductions, such as taxes or social insurance, are deposited each pay period to the legally stipulated accounts or agencies and as required by law. Other than legally mandated deductions, all other deductions from wages are made only with the express and written consent of the workers. Periodically evaluate how the wage you are providing meets the needs of workers and adjust wages to reflect changes in the cost of living.
summary: Requirements for wage transparency, timely payment, and the proper handling of legal and voluntary payroll deductions.
tags: payslips, minimum wage, payroll deductions, social insurance

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: Workers are not required to work more than the regular and overtime hours allowed by the law of the country where the workers are employed. All overtime work by workers is on a voluntary basis. Workers are entitled to at least 24 consecutive hours of rest in every seven-day period. If workers are required to work on a rest day due to a genuine need for continuity of production or service, workers must receive an equivalent period of compensatory rest immediately following. If the employment contract allows for contractual overtime, workers expressly agree to it. All overtime work is paid at least to the rate defined by law. Overtime should be used as an exception, and not the standard way you run your business. Document overtime and the workers’ expressed acceptance.
summary: Limits on working hours and requirements for voluntary overtime, premium pay, and mandatory weekly rest periods.
tags: overtime, voluntary work, rest periods, premium pay

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: Clear and effective policies and procedures are in place for occupational health and safety and are updated periodically. Occupational health and safety committees are created and their roles are clearly understood by all workers and managers. Ongoing safety training is provided to all personnel, including managers, supervisors, workers and security guards. All workers and other people who enter business premises are properly protected. The structural integrity and fire safety of worksites are specifically assessed and updated periodically. Appoint a senior member of management to administer and oversee your safety plan. Your plan should include safety incident and accident reduction targets. Examples of training might include: fire and electrical safety, confined space, hazardous chemicals and the use of personal protective equipment. Assess the potential impact of your activity on workers and the community and take steps to mitigate any negative impact.
summary: Mandatory requirements for OHS policies, safety committees, regular training, and structural/fire safety assessments.
tags: ohs committee, safety training, fire safety, hazard mitigation

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: Procedures provide effective, accessible channels for workers to complain, make suggestions and lodge grievances; and require the matter to be fully investigated and result in swift, unbiased and fair resolution. Grievance mechanisms channels are widely communicated and guarantee the confidentiality of any complainant (if so desired) and prohibit retaliation. Specific measures exist to protect complainants against victimisation. All managers are trained on the policy and procedures for the handling of complaints and grievances. Remedies are timely and open to appeal. Having multiple ways for workers to express issues or items of concern is recommended, and all mechanisms should be administered so that workers feel free to use them and have no concerns about retaliation. Data on the receipt and handling of grievances is maintained and analysed to ensure the efficacy of the grievance mechanisms.
summary: Requirements for accessible, confidential grievance channels that allow workers to raise concerns without fear of retaliation.
tags: grievance resolution, non-retaliation, confidentiality, worker voice

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: The rights and title to property and land of the individual, indigenous people and local communities are respected. All negotiations with regard to their property or land, including the use of and transfers of it, adhere to the principles of free, prior and informed consent, contract transparency and disclosure. A zero land grabbing policy is implemented. Land rights are relevant where land for your business needs to be acquired, leased or used. Ensure individuals responsible for land acquisition fully understand the impact of those changes and can demonstrate proper land title and contract transparency through assessment outcomes. Make certain you know what action to take and who needs to be consulted to ensure legal, environmental and social requirements are assessed and managed where land use changes are relevant.
summary: Policy requiring respect for land rights and the application of Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) in land transactions.
tags: fpic, land grabbing, indigenous rights, contract transparency

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: Environmental management policies and procedures are in place regarding water, energy, hazardous materials, air quality and emissions, deforestation, waste and other significant risks. All necessary current and valid legal permits are held for its operations. Training is provided to all relevant personnel to ensure knowledge of and compliance with all necessary legal permits. A systematic review of the supplier’s sustainability practices and environmental management systems is undertaken regularly with support from experienced conservationists and with the involvement of local communities. Have a business plan that includes clear environmental performance targets. Your company should have valid relevant permits for use and disposal of resources. Workers responsible for assessment and implementation of environmental targets must fully understand the minimum requirements of local, national and international law related to environmental standards.
summary: Requirement for suppliers to maintain valid environmental permits and implement management policies for water, energy, and waste.
tags: legal permits, ems, resource efficiency, environmental targets

doc_title: UNILEVER RESPONSIBLE SOURCING POLICY
chunk_text: Any failure to comply with this Policy of which the supplier is aware should be reported to Unilever as soon as possible. Failure to do so will be a breach of this RSP. We strongly support a culture of speaking up for both suppliers and their workers without fear of retaliation against those who report actual or suspected breaches. Unilever will investigate any concern raised and discuss findings with the supplier. The supplier shall assist with any such investigation and provide access to any information reasonably requested. If remediation is required, the supplier will devise and inform Unilever of their corrective action and implementation plans and timeline to effectively and promptly resolve the breach. Review your current practices against the Policy to ensure you are not at risk of any breaches.
summary: Mandatory requirement for suppliers to report policy breaches and cooperate with Unilever's investigations and remediation plans.

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: The Standards apply to suppliers of Walmart Inc. and suppliers of Walmart-controlled subsidiaries globally. Suppliers include anyone that provides products to Walmart, including goods for resale and for Walmart’s own use. A signed supplier agreement, acceptance of a purchase order, and/ or provision of merchandise to Walmart constitutes acceptance of these Standards and serves as the Supplier’s continuing affirmation of compliance. In addition, Walmart may enter into contracts with certain other parties that require those parties to comply with these Standards. In this document, we refer to anyone covered by the Standards as a “supplier.” Our suppliers include some of the largest and most well-known companies in the world as well as smaller companies providing product to a single store. They span the wide range of products we buy and sell.
source_section_or_page: Who is Covered by Our Standards, p. 5
summary: Definition of suppliers covered by the standards and the mechanism of mandatory acceptance via purchase orders.
tags: supplier agreement, purchase order, affirmation of compliance, onboarding

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: Suppliers are responsible for compliance with these Standards throughout their business and throughout the process of providing products to Walmart. This includes responsibility for the conduct of any suppliers, subcontractors, and agents they use as part of their Walmart business (including, for example, factories, processing facilities, and raw material, component, ingredient providers and labor recruitment agents). Anyone who violates the Standards may be subject to consequences, up to and including termination of business with Walmart. Walmart reserves the right to audit or inspect suppliers at any time to determine whether they are complying with these Standards. These Standards complement the Code of Conduct by applying Walmart’s values to our relationships with suppliers.
source_section_or_page: Who is Covered by Our Standards, pp. 5-6
summary: Mandatory supplier responsibility for the compliance of their own subcontractors and agents, backed by Walmart's right to audit.

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: The following issues should be reported immediately to Walmart Ethics & Compliance when related to a supplier’s business with Walmart: bribery; forced labor, prison labor, trafficked labor, child labor, and underage labor; violence against or harassment of workers; sanctions violations; producing products in a facility not approved for Walmart production; and government investigations or enforcement activities. Conditions posing an imminent risk to the health and safety of workers and incidents involving loss of life, significant disruption to operations, significant injury, and significant loss of property should be reported to the appropriate governmental authority in accordance with local requirements. These should also be reported to Walmart Ethics & Compliance. When in doubt, report issues to Walmart Ethics & Compliance. You can make anonymous reports to the Ethics & Compliance Helpline to the extent allowed by law.
summary: List of high-priority incidents and ethical violations that suppliers are required to report immediately to Walmart.
tags: ethics reporting, forced labor, bribery, facility approval

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: As a supplier, you should actively manage risk related to your business with Walmart by understanding and assessing risks relating to your industry, products, and workforce. Research and stay up to date on the laws, regulations, standards, industry best practices, conditions of sale, and scientific knowledge relevant to your products. Adopting strong operations, safety, and quality management systems is expected. Knowing your suppliers, subcontractors, and factories and monitoring their performance is required. Walmart has policies that require suppliers producing certain types of products—including private brand products, products bearing brands exclusive to Walmart, and products where Walmart will be the importer of record—to disclose to Walmart how and where those products are made and who is making them. Suppliers are required to understand these policies and comply with them to the extent applicable.
summary: Requirement for suppliers of private brands or imported products to disclose facility locations and production details.
tags: private brand, importer of record, risk management, facility disclosure

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: Suppliers must provide a mechanism for workers or other stakeholders to report concerns to management, to you as the supplier, and to third parties. These mechanisms should allow for anonymity and prohibit retaliation by you as the supplier against any germane party, including human rights organizations, for reporting in good faith. Walmart makes its Ethics & Compliance reporting channels available to workers who have concerns about suppliers and facilities that make product for Walmart. Suppliers of Walmart-branded product and product where Walmart will be the importer of record are required to distribute Walmart posters throughout their supply chain to help make workers aware of Walmart’s expectations and the availability of those reporting channels. Addressing reports that your management, employees, or subcontractors have engaged in harassment, threatening behavior, or discrimination is mandatory.
summary: Requirement for suppliers to establish anonymous grievance mechanisms and distribute Walmart's ethics posters in their supply chain.
tags: grievance mechanism, whistleblower, posters, non-retaliation

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: Recruit responsibly. Do not charge workers recruitment or similar fees—even if the collection of such fees is allowed under local law. If such fees are charged, we expect you to repay them. We also expect you to communicate to migrant workers the terms of their employment contract in their native language prior to departure from their home region. Allow workers freedom of movement. Do not keep workers’ personal identity documents or other valuable possessions, do not control workers’ freedom of movement through debts owed to you, brokers, or other third parties, and allow workers to terminate employment on reasonable notice. Workers’ inability to immediately access their personal identity documents restricts their movement. Providing personal locker space to workers can be a good way to secure valuable possessions. The costs of recruitment should be paid by the employer and not the worker.
source_section_or_page: Do Not Use Involuntary, Trafficked, Child, or Underage Labor, p. 10
summary: Prohibition of recruitment fees and identity document retention, with a requirement for native-language contracts for migrant workers.

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: Provide a safe, clean, and healthy work environment as appropriate for your industry, geography, and workforce. This includes ensuring facilities are structurally sound, fit for purpose, compliant with electrical and fire safety laws and standards, and well maintained. Provide access to clean and sanitary facilities and clean drinking water. Implement appropriate procedures and safeguards to prevent accidents and injuries to workers. Establish proper maintenance, monitoring, and inspection routines, worker training and protection, and fire safety measures. Take appropriate steps to protect workers from exposure to harmful chemicals, infectious disease, and other similar risks. Observe restrictions on hazardous work for young workers. Where you work alongside Walmart associates or in Walmart facilities, make sure you and your employees do not pose a risk to the safety of our associates and customers.
summary: Comprehensive OHS requirements covering facility integrity, fire safety, clean water, and protection from chemical hazards.
tags: facility integrity, fire safety, drinking water, chemical exposure

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: Our suppliers should help us maintain trust by providing us with products that meet all legal, industry, and Walmart safety, quality, and technical requirements. Implementing appropriate risk management systems to protect against food and product safety hazards is required. Suppliers should have these systems independently validated and verified. Monitoring products you produce for safety and quality and promptly reporting material issues to Walmart is mandatory. Material issues include failing to meet recognized safety standards and defects in product labeling or instructions that increase the risk of unsafe use. In the case of food products, material issues also include product specification deviations and microbiological, chemical or physical hazards that affect the safety of the product. Notify Walmart of voluntary and mandatory product recalls and removals where you identify products as not meeting applicable requirements.
source_section_or_page: Uphold High Standards for Safety and Quality, p. 12
summary: Requirement for suppliers to implement independently verified safety risk management systems and report material product defects.
tags: product safety, risk management, independent verification, quality standards

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: Walmart generally expects all suppliers’ plants to be certified to a Global Food Safety Initiative-benchmarked standard and we will ask you to provide evidence that your plant is certified. We may ask you to provide other evidence that you are managing food safety hazards effectively, including our expectations regarding compliance with our minimum product microbiological and chemical requirements. Finally, we expect you to report any safety issues to us immediately. As the supplier, you are responsible for ensuring that any claim you make about the product you are providing to us is true. You need to take steps to verify that any sustainability certification provided is genuine and that the product in fact meets the conditions of the certification. You as the supplier have the responsibility for following up on customer complaints and investigating whether the product is unsafe.
summary: Expectation for GFSI certification and a requirement for suppliers to verify the validity of any sustainability claims or certifications.
tags: gfsi, food safety, certification verification, sustainability claims

doc_title: STANDARDS FOR SUPPLIERS (Product Suppliers)
chunk_text: Establish controls to secure the supply chain from being used for improper purposes, including smuggling, terrorism, fraud, and theft. Walmart participates in the Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT) program in the United States and similar programs in other countries. Suppliers providing product where Walmart will be the importer of record are expected to exercise oversight in accordance with the security principles and requirements of these programs and to help Walmart maintain a safe and secure supply chain. Formulate and label products in a way that allows them to be transported, stored, and sold without compromising the products or the supply chain. Where the supplier is responsible for delivering product to Walmart, ensure containers and conveyances used are safe, sound, clean, and appropriate for the safe delivery of product to Walmart.
source_section_or_page: Observe Trade, Sanctions, and Security Laws and Guidelines, p. 13
summary: Requirement for suppliers to implement supply chain security controls aligned with international programs like CTPAT.
