doc_title: Simplified ESG Disclosure Guide (SEDG) Version 2
chunk_text: Waste can be generated in the company’s own activities or by entities upstream and downstream in the company’s value chain. Waste can have significant negative impacts on the environment and human health when inadequately managed. Disclosures require information on how the company prevents waste generation and how it manages waste that cannot be prevented. SEDG-E4.1: Report total waste in metric tonnes: Generated; Diverted from disposal; and Directed to disposal. The quantity, quality, and type of waste generated in the company’s own activities (e.g., during extraction, processing, procurement of materials) is to be disclosed. Destination of waste can include recycling operations such as downcycling, upcycling, or composting, and disposal operations such as incineration (with or without energy recovery) and landfilling.
summary: Requirement to report total waste generation and the breakdown of waste directed to recovery versus disposal streams.

doc_title: Simplified ESG Disclosure Guide (SEDG) Version 2
chunk_text: Healthy and safe work conditions involve both prevention of physical and mental harm, and promotion of workers’ health. This covers considerations around work-related hazards, ill health, and injuries. SEDG-S4.1: Report the number of fatalities and injuries in the company, if any. Work-related hazards and injuries are included as part of work-related injuries, covering both short-latency and long-latency ill health. High-consequence injuries such as fatalities are separately captured. A company which has no control over both the work and workplace still has a responsibility to make efforts, including any leverage it might have, to prevent and mitigate negative occupational health and safety impacts that are directly linked to its operations, products, or services by its business relationships. Ongoing safety training is pre-emptive and key to an effective management system.
source_section_or_page: Social: Occupational Health and Safety, pp. 9, 51-53
summary: Requirement to report occupational fatalities and injuries, including impacts linked to operations through business relationships.

doc_title: Simplified ESG Disclosure Guide (SEDG) Version 2
chunk_text: The inputs used to manufacture products can be non-renewable or renewable, composed of virgin or recycled materials. The company’s contribution to resource conservation can be indicated by its approach to recycling, reusing and reclaiming materials. SEDG-E5.2: Report the percentage of recycled input materials used to manufacture the company’s primary products and services. Recycled input materials are defined as materials that replace virgin materials, which are purchased or obtained from internal or external sources, and that are not by-products. The percentage is calculated as total recycled input materials used divided by total input materials used, multiplied by 100. The reporting company should exclude rejects and recalls of products. Data used must reflect the material in its original state and be clear if the figures are estimated or measured directly.
summary: Advanced requirement to report the percentage of recycled materials used in the manufacturing of primary products and services.

doc_title: Simplified ESG Disclosure Guide (SEDG) Version 2
chunk_text: Companies are expected to respect consumer privacy and take reasonable measures to ensure the security of personal data that they collect, store, process or disseminate. They are expected to limit collection to lawful and transparent means and not use personal information for purposes other than those agreed upon. SEDG-G5.1: Report the total number and nature of substantiated complaints received concerning breaches of customer privacy and loss of customer data, if any. Substantiated complaints can be from outside parties or regulatory bodies. In addition, the company can consider disclosing the total number of identified leaks, thefts, or losses of customer data. Management of customer data is becoming more critical globally, and companies need to ensure they are within all required limitations of their data use.

doc_title: Simplified ESG Disclosure Guide (SEDG) Version 2
chunk_text: Communication and training build internal and external awareness and the necessary capacity to combat corruption. Risk assessments help the company to design policies and procedures to combat corruption. SEDG-G4.2: Report the total number and percentage of employees who have received training on the company’s anti-bribery and anti-corruption policy. The communication and enforcement of the company’s anti-corruption and anti-bribery policies and procedures need to be consistent, pervasive and visible. The disclosure seeks to capture the extent and reach of training among all employees of the company. Ensuring employees fully understand and appreciate the value of good corporate governance processes through training and robust communication is a key recommendation for maintaining a culture of integrity.

doc_title: Simplified ESG Disclosure Guide (SEDG) Version 2
chunk_text: Access to fresh water is essential for human life and is recognised as a human right. The amount of water withdrawn by a company can impact ecosystems, local social and environmental contexts, and the needs of other water users. SEDG-E3.1: Report the total water withdrawn from all areas, and a breakdown of this total by type in litres: Purchased water (from municipal or private utilities); Surface water (naturally occurring lakes, rivers, harvested rainwater); Groundwater (recovered from underground); Seawater; and Produced water (entering as a result of extraction or processing raw materials). Through a comprehensive understanding of its water use, a company can assess its impacts. Companies are encouraged to prioritize action in areas with water stress and align their approaches with other water users.

doc_title: Sustainability Reporting Handbook For Vietnamese Companies
chunk_text: The “boundary” of the report is defined based on an assessment of which entities should be included for reporting. Typically, the company’s equity stake, organizational and operational control as well as ease of reporting incrementally on diverse entities constitute the basis for selecting the reporting boundary. At a minimum, the reporting organization should include entities over which the organization exercises control. These should be covered by Indicators of Operational Performance (emissions, waste, child labor, etc.). Entities over which the organization exercises significant influence should be covered by Disclosures on Management Approach (management systems, protocols followed, certifications etc.). For all material issues, the management approach and key performance indicators should be included in the report.
summary: Defines reporting boundaries based on control (operational performance) versus significant influence (management approach).

doc_title: Sustainability Reporting Handbook For Vietnamese Companies
chunk_text: Organizations should disclose the extent and performance of supply chain sustainability practices and risk management. This involves reporting on the various environmental and social aspects for reporting, with the degree of detail and the KPIs chosen varying depending on the importance of certain sectors and stakeholder interests. Key performance aspects and indicators listed in reporting standards can help to identify material issues. These need to be prioritized based on a combination of the company’s own view of what’s most important and relevant, and concerns expressed by stakeholders. Material sustainability considerations should also link directly to the company’s business model and its various interactions within the supply chain.

chunk_text: Organizations should report on their investment and procurement practices, specifically the percentage and total number of significant investment agreements that include human rights clauses or that have undergone human rights screening. chunk_text: Under Market Presence performance indicators, organizations are encouraged to report on their policy, practices and the proportion of spending on locally-based suppliers at significant locations of operation. By disclosing the extent to which the company prioritizes local hiring and local suppliers, it demonstrates its contribution to local economic development and the sustainability of its supply chain in the regions where it has a major presence or significant operations.

doc_title: Sustainability Reporting Handbook For Vietnamese Companies
chunk_text: A combination of internal and external factors should be used to determine whether information is material, including factors such as the organization’s overall mission and competitive strategy, concerns expressed directly by stakeholders, and the organization’s influence on upstream and downstream entities. Material information is any information that influences stakeholder assessments and decisions about the company. This is the same information the company management team would focus on when making decisions about the company’s future. Assessments of materiality should also take into account the basic expectations expressed in the international standards and agreements with which the organization is expected to comply, such as IFC performance standards or UN Global Compact.

doc_title: Sustainability Reporting Handbook For Vietnamese Companies
chunk_text: A “report or explain” framework is designed to encourage Vietnamese companies to start reporting. This means companies should report their environmental and social (E&S) performance or explain why they have chosen not to. Listed and soon-to-list companies are encouraged to include sustainability reporting as part of their holistic reporting, either within the annual report or separately. This guideline focuses on environmental and social aspects of business performance by considering the needs of companies listed on the Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh stock exchanges. It serves to highlight the basic disclosure requirements for a company to begin its reporting journey and meet investor and stock exchange requirements.

doc_title: Sustainability Reporting Handbook For Vietnamese Companies
chunk_text: Organizations should identify and disclose operations having significant risk for incidents of child labor and measures taken to contribute to the elimination of child labor. Similarly, they must report on operations identified as having significant risk for incidents of forced or compulsory labor and measures to contribute to the elimination of these practices. These indicators are part of Labor Management relations, which cover practices that foster amicable relations. Organizations should also disclose non-compliance with any of the International Labour Organization (ILO) core standards. For procurement professionals, this information is critical to understanding the ethical risks associated with a supplier's labor force and their adherence to international human rights standards.

doc_title: Sustainability Reporting Handbook For Vietnamese Companies
chunk_text: The Product Responsibility aspect covers the effects of products and services on customers and end users. This relates to practices ensuring customer health and safety, customer satisfaction, recall procedures, and customer data protection. Organizations should disclose the total number of substantiated complaints regarding breaches of customer privacy and losses of customer data. The disclosure would also need to incorporate any non-compliance events with applicable rules and regulations concerning health and safety impacts of products and services during their lifecycle. For enterprise buyers, understanding how a supplier manages data privacy and product safety is essential for mitigating operational and reputational risks within the procurement and supply cycle.

doc_title: Sustainability Reporting Handbook For Vietnamese Companies
chunk_text: Organizations should disclose their overall status on compliance with various rules and regulations on environmental performance as well as details of non-compliance, if any. Reporting should cover absolute and intensity of environmental emissions, effluent, and waste, as well as environmentally safe handling and disposal procedures. For procurement teams, this data serves as a benchmark for evaluating a supplier's operational compliance and their management of environmental impacts related to production.

doc_title: Sustainability Reporting Handbook For Vietnamese Companies
chunk_text: One of the ways to enhance stakeholder confidence in your report is to obtain third party assurance. Assurance is similar to the financial audit of an annual report. An assurance engagement will focus on the accuracy and completeness of the information in the sustainability report and the extent to which the report responds to stakeholder interests and concerns. Assurance for sustainability reports typically assesses the reliability of the underlying data systems that produced the data and content in the report. Choose a reputable assurance provider that can add value to your ongoing reporting activities. Sharing this update on your reporting journey shows stakeholders that you are transparent about, and committed to, continuous improvements.

chunk_text: IFC’s Sustainability Framework includes Performance Standards that apply to investee clients, providing guidance on how to identify and manage risks and impacts. Performance Standards cover eight aspects, including Assessment and Management of Environmental and Social Risks, Labor and Working Conditions, Resource Efficiency and Pollution Prevention, and Community Health, Safety and Security. Investee companies must meet the requirements in the IFC Performance Standards and World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines, and develop appropriate action plans prior to investment. During the life of an investment, companies must provide updates to IFC, as well as relevant stakeholders, on their adherence to the Performance Standards and any agreed action plans.
